newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK court OKs Mandarin Resources wind-up petition.
newsitem.headline: HK court OKs Mandarin Resources wind-up petition.

text.p: Hong Kong's Supreme Court ruled in favour of a petition by regulatory authorities seeking the liquidation of Mandarin Resources Corp Ltd, a court statement obtained by Reuters on Wednesday said.

Judge Anthony Rogers ruled on Tuesday the petition by the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) should stand despite objections from Mandarin and its controlling shareholder, legislator Chim Pui-chung, the statement said.
Last June, the SFC filed the petition with Hong Kong's Supreme Court on grounds that the firm's affairs were being conducted in a manner prejudicial to shareholders' interests.
Mandarin and Chim applied to the court for the petition to be struck out.

Chim has long been locked in a bitter row with the SFC over the winding up of the company. Trading in Mandarin Resources' shares on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong has been suspended for more than a decade.
Chim was arrested in July and charged with two counts of conspiracy to forge in connection with the property sales. He was released on bail and the case is still proceeding.
Chim was not immediately available for comment but local media quoted him as saying he was not surprised and would retain the right to appeal.
An SFC official said now that the court had turned down Chim's appeal to set aside the petition, a hearing would be held on the merits of the petition itself.
However, the official said no date had been set and Chim may still have further avenues of appeal.
